deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a set of reading notes, in Riemann's hand, excerpting and paraphrasing J. F. Herbart's philosophical writings. Its context is Riemann's documented study of Herbart, which also underlies the Naturphilosophie fragments.

The excerpts come from three places:
(a) 'Einleitung §. 247' and '§. 249', most likely Herbart's Lehrbuch zur Einleitung in die Philosophie.
  - §247: an odd agreement between idealism and empiricism. One takes the Ich as the source of all knowledge; the other takes sensation as the origin of the soul's primitive direction.
  - §249: an immature psychology obstructed metaphysics. Metaphysics was then confused with a 'Naturlehre des menschlichen Erkennens', which Herbart compares to confusing East and West Indies.
(b) A quotation from Herbart's 1822 essay 'Über die Möglichkeit und Nothwendigkeit, Mathematik auf Psychologie anzuwenden', cited as Werke Bd. VII, p. 152 (Hartenstein edition). Kant's merit was his striving for precision (Genauigkeit); without precision, philosophy teaching produces only 'Schwätzer und Thoren'. The next passage separates two questions, partly struck through by Riemann. 'How did a given representation arise in us?' belongs to psychology. 'How must it be reworked and used?' belongs to metaphysics; Riemann first wrote 'Mathematik' and corrected it. Mixing the two questions is named as the basic error of Kant's critique.
(c) Summaries of §§207–211 of a text with 'Cap. V. Von der allgemeinen Metaphysik' and 'Cap. VI. Von dem Verhältnisse der Metaphysik zu andern philosophischen Wissenschaften'. This is probably Herbart's Kurze Encyklopädie der Philosophie (1831).
  - §207: the double effect of Kant's doctrine of space. One effect was on matter and hence on Naturphilosophie; the other, earlier one was transcendental idealism.
  - §209: the four parts of general metaphysics:
    1. Methodologie: critique of the given and the 'Methode der Beziehungen'.
    2. Ontologie: the problems of inherence and change, which lead to the causal concept.
    3. Synechologie: principles of matter, with one section on space and one on time. It is the longest part and indispensable for Naturphilosophie.
    4. Eidolologie: investigation of the Ich, refutation of idealism, foundations of psychology.
  - §§210–211: metaphysics cannot found schools. Herbart rejects the view of metaphysics as 'first philosophy' and the Kantian replacement of metaphysics by critique of reason. 'False psychology is necessarily domineering' because it assumes concepts a priori. Herbart's own account follows: the concept of thing arises from complexions of marks; change contains a contradiction that common understanding resolves by the causal concept, hence the causal concept's necessity. Spatiality and temporality arise from a general law of reproduction (Psychologie als Wissenschaft II §109).

The whole lower block (§209 to Cap. VI heading) is crossed by a diagonal line. This is probably Riemann's mark that he had used or recopied the excerpt.

The only point of relevance to Riemann's mathematics is indirect. Herbart's synechology and his psychological genesis of space and time (as serial forms, 'Reihenformen') are known background to Riemann's Habilitationsvortrag. Riemann himself declared he was a Herbartian in psychology and epistemology but not in Naturphilosophie and metaphysics.
errors: No mathematical content, hence no mathematical errors. The excerpts appear to be faithful paraphrases of Herbart; no substantive misreporting detected.

results.what: Excerpts from Herbart on the division of metaphysics (Methodologie, Ontologie, Synechologie, Eidolologie) and on space/time arising from reproduction laws
results.modern_name: Herbartian metaphysics / psychological genesis of spatial and temporal series forms

results.what: Quotation from Herbart's 1822 essay on applying mathematics to psychology (precision as Kant's merit)

deep.surprise_reason: These are pure reading excerpts from Herbart, with no original mathematics. Riemann's close study of Herbart, and its influence on his ideas of space, is well documented (e.g. Scholz, Ferreirós). Note: 'already_credited_to_author' = 'yes' here refers to Riemann's known engagement with Herbart, not to authorship of the ideas, which are Herbart's.
transcription_corrections: 'Lehrformen [?]' should very likely read 'Reihenformen' (Herbart's term in Psychologie als Wissenschaft II §109 for spatial/temporal series forms).
'Spielt [?] es nur einzelne Bearbeitungen' probably reads 'Giebt es nur einzelne Bearbeitungen'.
'dass die Räthsel [?] den Begriff des Dinges herbeiführen' possibly 'dass die Complexionen den Begriff des Dinges herbeiführen' (uncertain).
In the separation-of-questions passage the struck word before 'Metaphysik' is 'Mathematik' (as transcribed) — the correction to 'Metaphysik' is Riemann's.
'Dort zusammen [?] ist die allgemeine Metaphysik' likely 'Dies zusammen [genommen] ist die allgemeine Metaphysik'.
The whole lower block from §209 to the Cap. VI heading is cancelled by a diagonal stroke, which the transcription does not indicate.
